# Milestone 1B-A - Home and Schedule verification

Implemented as an inactive, isolated genuine-Obsidian rehearsal. Stop for user review. This gate does not implement History/Statistics, pending-request recovery enhancements, migration or production activation.

## Delivered behavior

Exactly the twelve approved existing files were modified and ten approved files added. Home composes the existing legacy feed with the single explicitly bound native Project. It removes legacy rows only for that physical owner, preserves other legacy order and Resource ownership, and inserts native rows at the first excluded owner position (or appends when absent). Existing grouping, Necessity ordering, current/future/completed disclosure and civil-date helpers remain unchanged. Home Add keeps its existing legacy destination.

Native Home and Schedule actions use the existing M1A controller, application adapter and retained requests. They never resolve native references through Markdown. Schedule reuses the actual Overview, Week and Month renderers and existing compact Add/Edit forms. Calendar creation retains its selected date-only Due value, original operation and explicit task/Step identities across exact replay and reconstruction. Hidden continuation and Step bodies remain governed by the unchanged coherent-editor/form bridge. Nested trees, Phase-bound and recurring tasks are read-only; source navigation, clear-completed and native Roadmap are unavailable and reject before mutation. Modal whole-tree deletion remains distinct from clear-completed.

The only additional task-read fact is opt-in consumerFacts version 1 / recurrenceMember, computed in the existing authoritative capture. It is not an N0 DTO extension or a History projection. Default/v1 projections remain equivalent. Instrumented verification retains one authoritative capture and five domain validations. Native storage formats, commands, receipts, admission/recovery machinery, mutation adapters and retention files were not changed.

Unavailable native reads retain accepted presentation, disable native controls and withhold complete mixed/native counts. Known commitment survives failed refresh. Home composition brackets provider generations and bounds instability retries; it suppresses self-generated failure notifications during a demand. Schedule coalesces invalidations and does not continually retry its own unavailable reads. Disposal prevents late presentation. Existing legacy behavior remains the default when the optional dependency is absent.

The unchanged M1A recovery selection includes five actual parent-terminated children and their existing exact request/lock/death assertions. No durable-request or recovery format changed in this slice, so no new crash protocol or broad historical archive rerun was added. The prior immutable historical source-hash assertion remains untouched; its known current-versus-frozen-graph distinction is not represented as a newly green current historical runner. That unrelated historical selection was not rerun here.

The actual Home Tasks source sections and actual Project Schedule mount run in the existing isolated Electron/Obsidian host with genuine Plugin/Component/Modal APIs. This is not normal plugin onload or a complete Home dashboard startup. Other Home domains are excluded; History/Statistics explicitly show unavailable rather than incomplete totals. All process profiles, fixtures, native roots, request files, logs and staged builds are in verified OS Temp. No Itacan bundle was installed.

The final functional workflow exercises mixed owner feeds, Home legacy routing, native independent Step and parent complete/reopen, Edit Save, calendar creation/replay, Overview/Week/Month, known commitment with unavailable refresh, unavailable counts and host reconstruction. The final uninstrumented UI sample observed approximately 0.39 seconds to Overview and 1.27 seconds from calendar submit to form closure. Earlier samples were slower (approximately 1.1 / 3.4-4.7 seconds); window throttling and overlapping verification differ. These individual observations are not controlled benchmarks or a speedup claim.

## Failures retained and visual limitation

Initial new-test failures were fixture-only: a read fixture has no legacy toggle writer; retained access correctly refuses an unavailable authority; instrumentation must load before runtime; recurrence requires an explicit external reservation inventory; a declaration fixture accessed a pre-existing never-typed owner. Those tests now use the actual required seams without weakening the safety assertions.

Actual-host runs exposed a no-argument onCreated callback mismatch and a self-generated unavailable-refresh loop. Both were corrected in the approved consumer files. Original failed runs and committed request evidence remain in Temp. No uncertain operation was reissued with replacement identities. Later UI assertions were changed to await actual asynchronous unavailable publication, while retaining their rejection/count assertions.

Genuine modal API/DOM and form visibility/dimensions checks pass, and existing form/style source is unchanged. Hidden-window screenshots are unreliable for modal visual review: captured frames can show an older workspace or Obsidian onboarding/settings instead of the task modal. Disabling background throttling did not establish reliable modal captures. Therefore this gate does not claim pixel-perfect Add/Edit visual parity from those images. Actual Schedule dark styling, established toolbar and unavailable presentation were inspected. The screenshot limitation is retained explicitly for user review rather than masked with simulated images.

## Preservation and build comparison

The fresh baseline preserved twelve exact originals, dirty Git state and 1,779 protected/source/installed hashes. All twelve installed production assets remain identical. Baseline/final builds stayed in guarded Temp: main 171 factories, Atlas 24, identical factory IDs. Only home-task-read, task-workspace and task-view-primitives factories differ; all other staged assets match. Startup is unchanged, still has one Legacy Task Service construction, and imports no native integration package.

Observed drift occurred in .obsidian/workspace.json and subsequently .obsidian/plugins/hub-project-menu/data.json. Exact observed bytes and baseline/final hashes were preserved privately without restoration or actor attribution. All other inventoried nonallowlisted files match. No full protected-byte identity is claimed. Test execution was guarded against workspace filesystem mutations; no live-data write, real task mutation, migration, installation or production selection was performed.
